guidedTourSteps.label: Investor snapshot
guidedTourSteps.trigger: Open the product for the first time
guidedTourSteps.outcome: Understand the market problem, product scope, and rollout plan in under one minute.

guidedTourSteps.label: Secure onboarding
guidedTourSteps.trigger: Create users and send first-login access
guidedTourSteps.outcome: Each employee enters through role-based access, 2FA, and audit-friendly sessions.

guidedTourSteps.label: Project setup
guidedTourSteps.trigger: A new construction job is awarded
guidedTourSteps.outcome: The portal creates one source of truth for BOQ, phases, deadlines, team members, and progress.

guidedTourSteps.label: Daily field capture
guidedTourSteps.trigger: Work is completed on site today
guidedTourSteps.outcome: Supervisor input becomes an engineer-verified official report with photos and attachments.

guidedTourSteps.label: Management approval
guidedTourSteps.trigger: A report, document, material request, or invoice needs sign-off
guidedTourSteps.outcome: Approvals move through the right chain with comments, reminders, escalation, and audit records.

guidedTourSteps.label: Inventory & Stores
guidedTourSteps.trigger: Materials or tools move between warehouse and project site stores
guidedTourSteps.outcome: Warehouse/site stock, tagged tool location, approvals, suppliers, invoices, and costs become governed workflows instead of spreadsheets.

guidedTourSteps.label: Mobile execution
guidedTourSteps.trigger: Users work from site on low bandwidth
guidedTourSteps.outcome: A PWA-friendly flow keeps drafts, photos, approvals, and notifications usable on phones.

guidedTourSteps.label: Launch path
guidedTourSteps.outcome: The team has an MVP scope, acceptance scenarios, migration inputs, and deployment model.

productTourSteps.title: Start with the investor story
productTourSteps.body: This opening view explains the final product in plain business language before the viewer studies any module.
productTourSteps.instruction: Use this screen to frame the portal as one operating system for construction reporting, approvals, documents, materials, finance, and mobile work.

productTourSteps.title: Read the operations pulse
productTourSteps.body: The pulse card shows the kind of live management view investors expect from an enterprise SaaS product.
productTourSteps.instruction: Point out that approved field activity immediately updates KPIs, pending approvals, late updates, and document risk.

productTourSteps.title: Show the business problem
productTourSteps.body: The proposal explains what the company is replacing: chat follow-ups, spreadsheet tracking, unclear approvals, and document confusion.
productTourSteps.instruction: Use this section to make non-technical viewers feel the pain before showing the product solution.

productTourSteps.title: Prove executive value
productTourSteps.body: The value cards translate features into measurable operating outcomes: speed, control, trust, cost, and field adoption.
productTourSteps.instruction: Frame the product as a management operating layer, not only a reporting app.

productTourSteps.title: Follow the business flow
productTourSteps.body: This map connects project setup, field update, engineer verification, approval, and final business record.
productTourSteps.instruction: Walk stakeholders through this first so every later feature feels connected to the operating flow.

productTourSteps.title: Confirm requirements coverage
productTourSteps.body: Every documented module is mapped to prototype coverage and final-product behavior so stakeholders can see nothing important is missing.
productTourSteps.instruction: Use this when technical and non-technical reviewers ask whether the prototype reflects the documentation.

productTourSteps.title: Secure first login
productTourSteps.body: New users enter through a controlled sign-in flow with email, password, and 2FA for the MVP.
productTourSteps.instruction: Explain that Admin creates users, sends access, and the first login requires secure completion before role-based access opens.

productTourSteps.title: Show role-based permissions
productTourSteps.body: Every feature screen now starts with owner, trigger, user action, system action, and business result.
productTourSteps.instruction: Use this guide to explain how each module works without making investors read technical documentation.

productTourSteps.title: Track operational KPIs
productTourSteps.body: The dashboard summarizes active projects, pending approvals, late updates, documents, low stock, and unread alerts.
productTourSteps.instruction: Highlight that managers get live risk signals instead of waiting for spreadsheets or chat updates.

productTourSteps.title: Review project progress
productTourSteps.body: Project cards let managers switch between jobs and inspect progress, budget, deadlines, delayed reports, and discipline progress.
productTourSteps.instruction: Click a project to show how the prototype changes the detail panel while keeping the same workflow structure.

productTourSteps.title: Create the project baseline
productTourSteps.body: The final product starts each job with project code, BOQ import/manual entry, milestones, members, deadlines, and progress rules.
productTourSteps.instruction: Explain that all later reports, WIRs, costs, documents, and approvals connect back to this baseline.

productTourSteps.title: Explain BOQ and Gantt logic
productTourSteps.body: The Gantt-style timeline previews phase planning, owners, progress status, and delay visibility.
productTourSteps.instruction: Connect this to the BOQ baseline and approved quantities that drive real project progress later.

productTourSteps.title: Walk the daily report chain
productTourSteps.body: Supervisor updates become engineer-verified daily reports, then move to PM approval and automated PDF/email/archive.
productTourSteps.instruction: This is the most important MVP story: field data becomes an official company record.

productTourSteps.title: Show required report inputs
productTourSteps.body: The report form guides users through mandatory operational sections such as manpower, equipment, materials, safety, WIR, delays, photos, and attachments.
productTourSteps.instruction: Explain that this standardizes reporting and prevents incomplete daily records.

productTourSteps.title: Show report outcomes
productTourSteps.body: A completed report does more than save a form: it updates approval tasks, PDF/email export, audit, dashboard, and archive.
productTourSteps.instruction: This is the investor-grade story: the product turns field work into management evidence.

productTourSteps.title: Manage approval decisions
productTourSteps.body: Approvers see report, material, document, and invoice requests with route, SLA, status, and action buttons.
productTourSteps.instruction: Call out reject-with-reason, reminders, escalation, delegation, and audit trail as the management-control layer.

productTourSteps.title: Track inventory across stores
productTourSteps.body: The module separates central warehouses and project site stores so managers can see where stock is held before it is issued or consumed.
productTourSteps.instruction: Explain that the business no longer needs separate store ledgers to know what is in each warehouse or site.

productTourSteps.title: Review stock by location
productTourSteps.body: Consumable materials and tools show total, reserved, available, current location, and status across warehouse/site locations.
productTourSteps.instruction: Call out reserved quantity because approved requests should protect stock before physical issue.

productTourSteps.title: Locate tools and items
productTourSteps.body: Asset-tagged tools show their current warehouse/site, project, condition, status, and last movement.
productTourSteps.instruction: This directly answers the business question: where is this tool now, and can we issue it?

productTourSteps.title: Approve issue or transfer
productTourSteps.body: Issue and transfer requests move through approval before the Store Keeper updates stock and current location.
productTourSteps.instruction: Connect this to audit trail, cost visibility, and lower risk of missing tools or negative stock.

productTourSteps.title: Handle controlled documents
productTourSteps.body: Documents include type, project, revision, approval status, active/superseded versioning, and searchable metadata.
productTourSteps.instruction: Explain that field teams use active documents while managers retain version history and approval evidence.

productTourSteps.title: Preview document governance
productTourSteps.body: The prototype explains upload, review, active release, superseded warnings, and expiry reminders.
productTourSteps.instruction: Use this to reassure stakeholders that document control is not just file upload.

productTourSteps.title: Capture photo evidence
productTourSteps.body: Photos are limited, compressed, watermarked, queued for offline upload, and recoverable by Admin.
productTourSteps.instruction: Connect photo evidence back to the daily report and audit-ready project record.

productTourSteps.title: Preview financial control
productTourSteps.body: Finance previews budget-vs-actual, manpower cost, pending payment, invoices, payment status, and project P&L.
productTourSteps.instruction: Position this as Phase 2/3 value: cost visibility becomes connected to reports, materials, documents, and approvals.

productTourSteps.title: Trace invoice to P&L
productTourSteps.body: Invoices move from capture to accounts check, Operation Manager approval, payment status, and project cost rollup.
productTourSteps.instruction: This gives investors the finance expansion path without pretending OCR or full accounting is in the MVP.

productTourSteps.title: Explain alerts and reminders
productTourSteps.body: Notifications drive action for pending approvals, late reports, low stock, and active document updates.
productTourSteps.instruction: Show that the product actively moves work forward instead of depending on manual follow-up.

productTourSteps.title: Govern users and audit logs
productTourSteps.body: Admin can manage users and inspect audit logs while approved reports and historical identities remain protected.
productTourSteps.instruction: Explain the governance model: deactivate users, preserve records, audit overrides, and avoid silent edits.

productTourSteps.title: Show governance controls
productTourSteps.body: The portal preserves identity history, controls overrides, and keeps queryable audit evidence for sensitive actions.
productTourSteps.instruction: This is where technical reviewers see the product has real enterprise governance thinking.

productTourSteps.title: Show the field mobile flow
productTourSteps.body: The phone preview shows site users saving updates, queueing photos, and syncing when the connection allows.
productTourSteps.instruction: Use this to make the end product feel practical for construction sites, not only desktop offices.

productTourSteps.title: Explain offline execution
productTourSteps.body: Mobile behavior covers offline drafts, camera capture, photo queue, sync, autosave, approvals, and active document view.
productTourSteps.instruction: Close the adoption concern: the people on site can actually use it.

productTourSteps.title: Close with delivery confidence
productTourSteps.body: Delivery cards show hosting, environments, deployment, backups, testing, migration, and acceptance scenarios.
productTourSteps.instruction: End here so investors understand the prototype maps directly to implementation scope and launch readiness.

walkthroughSteps.title: Create project baseline
walkthroughSteps.detail: Admin/Operation Manager creates project, BOQ, milestones, members, and deadlines.

walkthroughSteps.title: Supervisor submits field update
walkthroughSteps.detail: Attendance, work location, OT, progress, safety, and five site photos are captured.

walkthroughSteps.title: Engineer verifies and submits report
walkthroughSteps.detail: Engineer validates quality/WIR status, adds work summary, and submits official report.

walkthroughSteps.title: Project Manager approves
walkthroughSteps.detail: PM approves, rejects with comments, or lets the system escalate after SLA breach.

walkthroughSteps.title: System updates records
walkthroughSteps.detail: Dashboard, PDF export, email notification, audit log, documents, and costs update.
